what_happened: On a multi-lane highway after handoff, the ego braked hard (17 to 8 m/s) for no clear reason and steered left out of its lane, though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its front hit actor 1 in the adjacent left lane. The hard braking probably also led to the later rear contact.

After handoff the ego braked hard for no clear reason on a highway with no hazard, slowing from about 17 to 8 m/s, and its planned path veered left toward the adjacent lane. Its front-left then struck actor 1, which was passing in the left lane. The ego was also rear-ended at some point.

On a straight multi-lane highway, after taking over at 4.6 s the policy braked hard (17 → 8.8 m/s) and its planned path veered left into the next lane, where vehicle 1 was driving alongside. The ego's front hit vehicle 1 at 6.2 s, while the recorded human path stayed straight in the original lane. The later rear contact came after this collision and probably resulted from the ego's unneeded hard braking.

The route said STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, but after the policy took over, its planned path bent left toward the next lane while it slowed from about 5.7 to 4.1 m/s. Pickup 41 was passing on the left at the same time. The ego drifted across the lane line, and its front hit the rear-right of the pickup as the pickup moved ahead.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned route bent right toward the human's lane, but the policy held a straight-to-slightly-left course while slowing from 12 to 7 m/s. It drove over the left lane boundary onto the landscaped median, ending about 7 m left of the recorded path; no other actor was nearby.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded human path curved right. Instead, the policy planned a path that went straight and slightly left while slowing from 10 to 7 m/s. The ego drifted off the left edge of the roadway onto the dirt median before the intersection, about 7.3 m from the human path; no other actor was involved.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded human path moved right across the lanes. The ego instead kept going straight on the far-left shoulder next to the median barrier, speeding up from 6.7 to 8.1 m/s, and drifted off the drivable area at 11.5 s, about 7.4 m from the recorded path. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clear enough to show the shoulder and barrier.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy braked hard (28.8 to 12.9 m/s) for no clear reason and drifted left onto the median shoulder, even though the command was RIGHT and the planned path went right. While it slowed, a following car (actor 40) caught up and was overlapping the ego's right-front at the moment it left the road. The run also logged a rear contact, but I couldn't see when it happened in these frames.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, but after taking over the policy held a straight-to-left heading. It slowed from 12 to 7 m/s and drifted left over the lane edge onto the landscaped median, ending about 7 m from the human's path.

The ego was on a multi-lane highway at about 27 m/s with nothing close ahead, yet it braked hard (down to 12.7 m/s, and something hit its rear along the way). Its planned path also bent left, away from the recorded path, which moved right as the command changed to RIGHT. By 8.0 s it had crossed the left edge line onto the shoulder by the median, about 5 m from the recorded path.
